title: Oi Muchim Spicy Cucumber Banchan
shortDescription: Crisp cucumber is salted briefly and tossed with gochugaru, rice vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, scallion, sesame oil, and sesame seeds just before serving.
culturalContext: Oi muchim is a quickly seasoned Korean cucumber banchan rather than a stuffed kimchi. The balance of chile, tang, sweetness, and sesame differs by household and by what accompanies it; this draft favors a bright, lightly sweet profile.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.item: Korean, Persian, or small pickling cucumbers

instructions.heading: Wash and slice
instructions.action: Wash and dry cucumbers, trim the ends, and slice evenly. Thinly slice the onion and scallions with clean tools.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cucumber slices are crisp and evenly thick with no soft spots.
instructions.safetyNote: Wash produce under cool running water and use a clean board.

instructions.heading: Salt briefly
instructions.action: Toss cucumber with salt and rest 10 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Moisture beads on the slices but they remain rigid and crisp.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the bowl away from raw meat and seafood preparation areas.

instructions.heading: Drain
instructions.action: Drain in a clean colander for 5 minutes and blot gently; do not squeeze or rinse.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices are moist but no liquid pools beneath them.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a sanitized colander and clean towel or disposable paper towels.

instructions.heading: Mix the dressing
instructions.action: In a clean bowl, stir gochugaru, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, sesame oil, and sesame seeds until the sugar begins to dissolve.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The dressing is glossy and evenly red.
instructions.safetyNote: Declare soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame allergens.

instructions.heading: Toss
instructions.action: Add cucumber, onion, and scallions and toss gently until evenly coated.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Every piece is lightly coated and the cucumber edges remain crisp.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean utensils and a clean serving dish.

instructions.heading: Serve immediately
instructions.action: Transfer to a serving dish and serve at once for maximum crunch, or cover and refrigerate briefly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Only a small amount of dressing has collected at the bottom.
instructions.safetyNote: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours at or below 40°F / 4°C.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan does not use a grill.
visualDonenessCues: Cucumber slices stay crisp after brief salting
Sugar is mostly dissolved in the dressing
Finished salad is glossy without excessive pooled liquid
foodSafetyNotes: Wash cucumbers and aromatics under cool running water before cutting.
Use clean tools, colander, bowl, and serving utensils.
Declare soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame allergens.
Serve promptly and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Discard if the cucumber becomes slimy or develops an off odor.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify soy sauce and gochugaru labels and prevent shared-utensil cross-contact.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying the label.
Persian or small pickling cucumbers can replace Korean cucumbers; avoid waxed slicing cucumbers.
ingredientSourcing: Choose small, firm, unwaxed cucumbers with no wrinkling or soft spots.
Use unseasoned rice vinegar so salt and sugar remain controllable.
makeAhead: Mix the dressing up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate; slice and season cucumbers close to serving.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container and use within 2 days; texture is best immediately and the limit requires food-safety review.
reheating: Do not reheat; serve cold or cool.
leftovers: Drain and add properly refrigerated leftover oi muchim to a cold rice bowl within the approved storage window.
servingSuggestions: Serve immediately with rice and grilled dishes
Spoon lightly so excess dressing remains in the serving bowl

faq.question: Why salt the cucumber first?
faq.answer: A short salting draws off surface moisture and seasons the slices while preserving their crisp center.

faq.question: Can I make oi muchim ahead?
faq.answer: The dressing can be made ahead, but toss it with cucumber near serving to limit watery softening.
